_metadata.description: OSINT reconnaissance techniques for the Recon phase of an AUTHORIZED intelligence-led engagement, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK Reconnaissance (TA0043). Every offensive technique is paired with a defensive counter-measure and a detection signal, so the same data drives both the emulation plan and the target's footprint-reduction plan.
_metadata.usage: Passive techniques only unless active recon is explicitly authorized in the signed scope/RoE. This models an authorized red team's recon; it is not a tool for profiling non-consenting individuals or organizations.

recon_techniques.name: Domain & DNS enumeration
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Subdomains, mail servers (MX), SPF/DMARC records, hosting providers, forgotten dev/staging hosts
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Audit external DNS for stale/dev records; remove wildcard leaks; monitor certificate transparency for unexpected subdomains issued under your domain
recon_techniques.detection_signal: Largely undetectable (passive) — the defensive move is footprint reduction, not detection

recon_techniques.name: WHOIS & registration data
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Registrant org, registration dates, name servers, sometimes contact emails/phone
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Use WHOIS privacy/registrar proxy; use role accounts not personal emails for registration

recon_techniques.name: TLS certificate transparency mining
recon_techniques.mitre_name: Search Open Technical Databases: Digital Certificates
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Every hostname a cert was ever issued for — including internal-sounding names and pre-launch services
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Avoid putting internal hostnames in public certs; use wildcard certs sparingly; monitor CT logs for your domains
recon_techniques.detection_signal: Undetectable (passive); CT monitoring detects mis-issuance, not the adversary's lookup

recon_techniques.name: Internet scan database lookup
recon_techniques.mitre_name: Search Open Technical Databases: Scan Databases
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Exposed services, open ports, banners, software versions — WITHOUT touching the target (someone else scanned)
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Reduce external attack surface; close unneeded ports; strip version banners; register for Shodan alerts on your own IP ranges
recon_techniques.detection_signal: Undetectable by the target (the scan was done by the database, not the adversary)

recon_techniques.name: Active port / service / vulnerability scanning
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Live open ports, service versions, exploitable vulnerabilities on in-scope hosts
open_sources: Direct interaction with authorized in-scope targets only
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Network IDS/IPS, rate-limiting, external attack-surface management, honeypots/canaries
recon_techniques.detection_signal: DETECTABLE — perimeter IDS, firewall logs, and connection-rate anomalies should fire. A blue-team drill: did scanning of in-scope hosts generate an alert?

recon_techniques.name: Email address & naming-convention harvesting
recon_techniques.mitre_name: Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Valid email format (first.last@), distribution lists, who works there — the raw material for phishing target lists
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Security-awareness training; DMARC enforcement; reduce public posting of individual addresses; use contact forms over exposed mailboxes
recon_techniques.detection_signal: Undetectable (passive); the defense is phishing-resistance downstream, not recon detection

recon_techniques.name: Breach-corpus / credential-exposure review
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Which corporate emails appear in public breach datasets (password reuse risk)
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Enforce MFA everywhere (kills reuse value); monitor your own domains in HIBP; force resets on exposed accounts; deploy a password blocklist
recon_techniques.detection_signal: Undetectable (passive); mitigated by MFA + credential monitoring

recon_techniques.name: Public code repository & secrets review
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Leaked API keys, internal hostnames, hardcoded creds, tech stack, CI/CD config in public repos and commit history
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Secret scanning (pre-commit + server-side); rotate any exposed secret; audit org members' public repos; use .gitignore for config
recon_techniques.detection_signal: Undetectable at the target; secret-scanning YOUR OWN repos is the control (see this repo's security-check workflow)

recon_techniques.name: Social media & employee profiling
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Org chart, technologies used (from job posts), employee roles — inputs for pretext/social-engineering scenarios
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Guidance on what staff share publicly; sanitize job posts of specific tech/version detail; security-awareness on pretexting
recon_techniques.detection_signal: Undetectable (passive); mitigated by awareness training and help-desk verification procedures

recon_techniques.name: Organizational & business-tempo profiling
recon_techniques.mitre_name: Gather Victim Org Information: Business Tempo
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Working hours, key dates, vendors/suppliers, physical locations — timing and pretext for an attack
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Heightened vigilance around publicly-known high-tempo periods (earnings, launches); vendor-impersonation awareness

recon_techniques.name: Victim-owned website content review
recon_techniques.what_it_reveals: Staff directory, technology hints (headers, JS), document metadata, exposed directories
open_sources: The target's own public website (browsing only)
recon_techniques.defensive_counter: Strip document metadata before publishing; remove verbose server headers; audit for exposed directories/backup files
recon_techniques.detection_signal: Low — high-volume crawling may show in web logs, but normal browsing is indistinguishable
